facts.statement: Xinjiangtitan lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now northwestern China.
facts.quote: lived during the Middle Jurassic of what is now Xinjiang, northwestern China

facts.statement: The generic name Xinjiangtitan is derived from the region of Xinjiang and the Greek word for giant, titan.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Xinjiang, and from titan, giant in Greek mythology

facts.statement: The specific name shanshanesis is derived from the county of Shanshan, named after the ancient Shanshan Kingdom.
facts.quote: The specific name, shanshanesis, is derived from an alternative name for the county where it was found, Shanshan, named after the ancient Shanshan Kingdom

facts.statement: The fossil was originally thought to be from the Late Jurassic Qigu Formation but is now assigned to the Middle Jurassic Qiketai Formation.
facts.quote: The specimen was originally reported as being from the Qigu Formation (Late Jurassic), but it was subsequently considered to be from the Qiketai Formation (Middle Jurassic)

facts.statement: Xinjiangtitan has the longest complete neck ever discovered for any animal, measuring nearly 15 meters with all 18 vertebrae present.
facts.quote: The neck, of which all 18 vertebrae are present, is nearly 15 m long and is the longest complete neck ever discovered of any animal

facts.statement: Xinjiangtitan is diagnosed by traits including a ventral keel on the penultimate cervical vertebra, elongated cervical vertebrae, a specific sacricostal yoke structure, and an extremely robust femur.
facts.quote: Xinjiangtitan was diagnosed based on the following traits: the presence of a ventral keel on the penultimate cervical centrum that forms a small semicircular process under the distal articular facet; both cervical vertebrae are relatively elongated; the sacricostal yoke except the first sacral rib; and an extremely robust femur

facts.statement: The series of dorsal vertebrae in Xinjiangtitan measures 3.72 meters in length.
facts.quote: The series of dorsal vertebrae has a length of 3.72 m

facts.statement: The femur of Xinjiangtitan is 1.65 meters long and the tibia is 0.98 meters long.
facts.quote: The femur is 1.65 m long, and the tibia is 0.98 m long

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Xinjiangtitan as the sister taxon of Mamenchisaurus.
facts.quote: Among sauropods, the phylogenetic analysis from its description places Xinjiangtitan as the sister taxon of Mamenchisaurus, the only other mamenchisaurid included

facts.statement: Xinjiangtitan shares derived characters with diplodocids, such as a prominent ambiens process of the pubis, a relatively short hind limb, and a caudomedially developed fourth trochanter on the femur.
facts.quote: Xinjiangtitan shares several derived characters with diplodocids, including prominent ambiens process of pubis, relatively short hind limb and fourth trochanter on the femur that is caudomedially developed

facts.statement: Xinjiangtitan lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 165 to 164 million years ago during the Callovian stage.
facts.quote: vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 165 a 164 millones de años durante el Calloviense

facts.statement: The type specimen of Xinjiangtitan shanshanesis was discovered in 2012 by a joint expedition of Jilin University, Shenyang Normal University, and the Xinjiang Geological Survey Institute.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Xinjiangtitan shanshanesis fue descubierto por una expedición conjunta de la Universidad de Jilin, la Universidad Normal de Shenyang y el Instituto de Estudios Geológicos de Xinjiang en 2012

facts.statement: Described in 2021, the neck of Xinjiangtitan, which contains all 18 vertebrae, measures nearly 15 meters and is the longest complete neck ever discovered for any animal.
facts.quote: Descrito en 2021, el cuello, del cual están presentes las 18 vértebras, mide casi 15 metros de largo y es el cuello completo más largo jamás descubierto de cualquier animal

facts.statement: Xinjiangtitan was one of the longest known sauropods, with a neck measuring at least 14.9 meters in length.
facts.quote: Xinjiangtitan fue uno de los saurópodos más largos conocidos, con un cuello largo que medía al menos 14,9 metros de largo

facts.statement: The series of dorsal vertebrae in Xinjiangtitan has a length of 322 centimeters.
facts.quote: La serie de vértebras dorsales tiene una longitud de 322 centímetros

facts.statement: The femur of Xinjiangtitan is about 165 centimeters long, and the tibia is 98 centimeters long.
facts.quote: El fémur tiene unos 165 centímetros de largo, y la tibia 98 centímetros

facts.statement: The time range for Xinjiangtitan is estimated from the Bathonian to the Tithonian (168.2 to 143.1 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Tithonian (168.2 to 143.1 million years ago)
